_comment: sim-robust-collect-stow-stall-v1 (coldliveapproach). Purpose: prove the post-release collect STOW survives a move_group PLANNER CRASH/HANG -- it completes to transport_ready when the planner is healthy, and FAILS FAST with a NAMED cause (never the opaque 120-sim-s 'phase timeout: stow') when it is not. Root cause: in coldliveapproach move_group SIGABRT'd ('malloc_consolidate(): invalid chunk size', host-stack.log:13869) at the retreat_tuck->stow boundary and did NOT respawn (zero move_group output after). The stow plan goal went to the dead /move_action server; goal ACCEPTANCE (a pacing-independent ms handshake) never returned, so the port sat in plan_accept until PR 228's SIM-clock planning deadline (PLAN_SIM_DEADLINE_S=30 sim-s) fired 4x and the controller looped STAGED_MOVE_RETRY to the 120-sim-s collect phase timeout. A SIGABRT-hung move_group keeps server_is_ready()==True (no clean DDS deregistration), so _handle_server_crash stayed inert, and _should_deadline_crash_retry is gated on clock=='wall' -- unreachable now PR 228 put every planning deadline on the SIM clock -- so the fm404 belt-and-braces crash recovery could never fire. The passing sibling (hosttimers) had ZERO move_group crashes, so the stall is this crash, NOT the masked_depth economy publish interval (economy never feeds the plan_accept budget).
_fix: A SIM-clock PLANNING-state deadline (plan_accept/plan_result) is now treated as positive evidence of a dead/hung move_group (PR 228's own rationale: healthy planning consumes ~1-2 sim-s, so the full sim budget elapsing with the goal never accepted / plan never returned is a hang). ros_adapter.RosMotionPort._poll re-sends the plan a bounded RESTOCK_PLAN_ACCEPT_CRASH_RETRY_MAX times (so a genuine crash+respawn whose server stale-reads ready still recovers -- the fm404 belt-and-braces, now reachable on the sim clock), then sets last_fault_was_planner_unrecoverable(); the controller (_planner_crash_failfast_or_none, checked before every move 'failed' retry) fails the op FAST with a named cause: '<phase> aborted: the move_group planner crashed or hung ... and did not respawn -- failing fast'. CPU-proven in tests/test_restock_collect_stow_stall.py.
_default_on: The fix is ON by default -- no new config key is needed in the mission JSON. RESTOCK_PLAN_ACCEPT_CRASH_RETRY_MAX (env, default 1) is the ONLY tunable: 1 => one recovery re-send then fail (2 x PLAN_SIM_DEADLINE_S = ~60 sim-s, well under the 120-sim-s collect phase timeout); 0 => fail on the first sim planning deadline. A healthy run never reaches a sim planning deadline, so this is inert there (byte-identical).
_bounded_gpu_proof: Run a COLLECT-ONLY mission under the FULL coldliveapproach keys with economy ON. Starting from the coldliveapproach run config (~/datasets/twin-robot-in-store-boot-v1/mission/mission-runtime-coldlive-approach.json; do NOT edit that file -- copy it): keep transfer_mode live_pose, masked_depth.economy {resolution_scale:0.5, publish_interval_s:0.1}, RESTOCK_HEARTBEAT_UNAVAILABLE_S=120, and ADD --stop-after collect so the run ends at the end of the collect op (stow + verify), not at couple. Invoke scripts/run_mobile_restock.py under /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, --heavy-threshold-mb 2500 for the always-on whispr (pid 1339, ~2.2 GB VRAM -- never touch it), never --force, never the hard Blender gate. Leave RESTOCK_PLAN_ACCEPT_CRASH_RETRY_MAX at its default (1).
_pass: PASS = the collect STOW completes to transport_ready (action=collect status=succeeded transport_ready=True), with NO 'phase timeout: stow'. If move_group crashes during the run, EITHER it respawns and the bounded crash re-send recovers the stow (one or more MOVE_GROUP_CRASH_RETRY 'plan ... sim-deadline' lines, then stow completes), OR it stays dead and the op ends FAST with 'PLANNER_UNRECOVERABLE' in host-stack.log + MANIP_HOST_FAILED reason '... move_group planner crashed or hung ... failing fast' (a named cause in mission.json), NOT the opaque 120-sim-s phase timeout. The named-fail outcome is an acceptable PASS of THIS deliverable (fail-fast-by-named-cause); the move_group heap crash itself is upstream (MoveIt/cuMotion octomap-clear, data-race class 'malloc_consolidate'/'unaligned tcache chunk') and is not fixable in the host.
_fail: FAIL = the stow still consumes the full per-phase timeout with the opaque 'phase timeout: stow' (the fix did not engage -- check that the run is on this branch and PLAN_ACCEPT_CRASH_RETRY_MAX is not forced to a huge value), OR a DIFFERENT move/phase now regresses (capture its host-stack.log line: the fired-deadline clock+state, the MOVE_GROUP / PLANNER line, and the controller HOST_FAULT_ESTOP reason).
